back: if + present simple, present simple: for facts and things that always happen.
notes: If you heat ice, it melts.

back: if + present simple, will + base verb: for real, likely future situations.
notes: If it rains, we will stay inside.

back: if + past simple, would + base verb: for imagined or unlikely present or future situations.
notes: If I were rich, I would build a clinic.

back: if + past perfect, would have + past participle: for an imagined past that did not happen.
notes: If I had known, I would have helped.

back: if + past perfect, would + base verb: a past condition with a present result.
notes: If I had slept, I would not be tired now.

back: If ... not. Do not add another negative after it.
notes: Unless you hurry = If you do not hurry.
If he comes (not will come); If I had known (not would have known).

back: + past simple (present), + past perfect (past), + would (annoying habits of others).
notes: I wish I lived nearer. I wish I had gone. I wish he would stop.

back: provided (that), providing, as long as, on condition that.
notes: You may go as long as you finish your chores.
